title: Medicare Scam Calls Threaten to Cancel Benefits
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare, saying your benefits will be canceled unless you give them personal information or pay a fee. They may use urgent language to scare you into acting quickly.
example_message: "This is Medicare. Your benefits will be canceled if you do not verify your Social Security number and bank account right now."
red_flags: Caller says your benefits will be canceled immediately
They ask for your Social Security or bank information
They pressure you to act right away
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you are concerned.

title: Fake Package Delivery Texts
how_it_works: You get a text saying a package couldn’t be delivered and you must click a link to reschedule or pay a fee. The link leads to a fake website that steals your information or installs malware.
example_message: "Your package is waiting for delivery. Please confirm your address and pay $1.99 to reschedule: [fake link]"
red_flags: Unexpected text about a delivery you didn’t order
Links that look strange or don’t match the delivery company
Requests for payment or personal information
what_to_do: Do not click the link—delete the message and contact the delivery company using their official website or phone number.

title: Social Security Email Phishing
how_it_works: You receive an email that looks like it’s from the Social Security Administration, saying there’s a problem with your account. The email asks you to click a link or open an attachment to fix the issue, but it’s a trick to steal your information.
example_message: "We have detected suspicious activity on your Social Security account. Please click here to verify your information."
red_flags: Links or attachments asking for personal details
what_to_do: Do not click any links—go to the official Social Security website or call them directly if you have concerns.

title: Romance Scams on Facebook
how_it_works: A scammer pretends to be interested in a romantic relationship on Facebook or other social media. After gaining your trust, they ask for money for an emergency or travel.
example_message: "I care about you so much, but I need help with a sudden medical bill. Can you send me $500?"
red_flags: Someone you’ve never met asks for money
Stories about emergencies or needing help
Refusal to meet in person or video chat
what_to_do: Never send money to someone you haven’t met in person, no matter how convincing their story is.

title: Grandparent Emergency Scam
how_it_works: A caller pretends to be your grandchild or someone calling for them, saying they’re in trouble (like in jail or in an accident) and need money right away. They may beg you not to tell anyone else.
example_message: "Grandma, I’m in trouble! I need you to send money for bail, but please don’t tell Mom or Dad."
red_flags: Caller claims to be a family member in urgent trouble
They want you to send money immediately, often by wire or gift card
what_to_do: Hang up and call your grandchild or another family member directly to check if the story is true.
